lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: graphing rational functions and identifying asymptotes
lessonRef.title: Transfer challenge: graphing rational functions and identifying asymptotes

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different context than the problems below.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A polynomial has degree 5 and leading coefficient -6. Describe its end behaviour.
choices: the left end falls and the right end rises
the left end rises and the right end falls

items.prompt: For f(x) = (x + 7) / (x + 3), state the vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote.
Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −3(x − 1)² − 9, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is -8. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?
The function f(x) = 2(x + 5)² − 9 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.
A polynomial has degree 2 and leading coefficient -5. Describe its end behaviour.
choices: the left end falls and the right end rises
the left end rises and the right end falls

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: These are meant to be hard. Show the reasoning even if you do not finish.

items.prompt: For f(x) = (x + 7) / (x + 8), state the vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −2(x + 5)² + 3, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is 7. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: The function f(x) = 3(x − 7)² − 9 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
